title: Power Automate process mining: import star schema (normalised) event data
summary: Hold: the OneLake control incorrectly says automation is not documented, although Microsoft documents an API that updates tenant settings. The import instructions, roadmap dates and licensing figures are supported; the blanket statement about pointing a process at any storage location should be narrowed.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Process Mining can ingest normalized event data without first flattening it into one wide table.
claims.quote: Power Automate Process Mining can ingest event data that isn't stored as a single wide table.

claims.claim: The star schema has an event table and an optional case table.
claims.quote: This article walks you through importing event data laid out as a **star schema** (one Event table + optional Case table + lookup tables) into Power Automate Process Mining, from the UX side.

claims.claim: Lookup tables are connected through foreign keys.
claims.quote: a *star schema*—a thin event table plus optional case and lookup tables, linked by foreign keys.

claims.claim: OneLake/Fabric sources can be managed Delta tables or loose Parquet or CSV files under Files/ in a lakehouse.
claims.quote: **OneLake / Microsoft Fabric**: A lakehouse with managed Delta tables, or loose Parquet or CSV files under the `Files/` area.

claims.claim: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 containers with CSV, Parquet or Delta-Parquet folders are supported.
claims.quote: **Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2**: A container with CSV, Parquet, or Delta-Parquet folders.

claims.claim: The normalized import formats are CSV, Parquet and Delta-Parquet.
claims.quote: | File formats | CSV, Parquet, Delta-Parquet | CSV, Parquet, Delta-Parquet |

claims.claim: A JSON configuration describes the source tables.
claims.quote: It declares the storage backend (ADLS Gen2 or OneLake), the file format (CSV, Parquet, or Delta-Parquet), and a list of **datasets**. Each dataset is one physical table.

claims.claim: The JSON configuration specifies the storage backend.
claims.quote: It declares the storage backend (ADLS Gen2 or OneLake), the file format (CSV, Parquet, or Delta-Parquet), and a list of **datasets**.

claims.claim: The JSON maps physical columns to Process Mining attributes.
claims.quote: It maps physical columns (or joined columns from lookup tables) to logical roles: case ID, activity, start timestamp, end timestamp, resource, finance metric, custom dimension, and more.
